clue.text: Authorised new driver to get nasty

parts.note: L is a learner driver's plate, so it stands for a new driver
nasty and awful both mean very unpleasant

explanation.surface: A newly licensed motorist turns aggressive on the road despite being officially permitted to drive.
explanation.walkthrough: L comes from the L-plate a British learner driver must display.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lawful is permitted by law, which is to say legally sanctioned.

clue.text: Mischievous when the month starts late

indicators.note: the month's start arrives too late to be included, so its opening letter is dropped

parts.note: March is a month of the year

explanation.surface: A remark that someone is up to mischief when spring arrives behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts late' removes the M from MARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch look or smile is knowingly playful, a synonym of roguish or impish.

clue.text: Stopping: not out to prolong outdoor hobby

indicators.note: the hobby is lengthened by having another piece placed inside it

parts.note: fishing is a pastime enjoyed outdoors
in is the opposite of out, as a batter still in at cricket

explanation.surface: Someone stops a game being called off to keep enjoying their favourite pastime outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Finishing means bringing to a halt or completing, the same as stopping.

clue.text: A trail churned up by a horse catcher

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are stirred into a new order like churned ground

explanation.surface: A horse rounding up cattle leaves a muddy path behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'churned up' rearranges ATRAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is a lasso, a rope with a noose used to catch horses and cattle.

clue.text: A quiet farm with house for Peggy

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
a croft is a small farm with a dwelling, especially in Scotland

explanation.surface: A request for a peaceful smallholding with a cottage for someone named Peggy.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Peggy Ashcroft was a celebrated British actress.
explanation.definitionFit: The forename identifies the stage actress Dame Peggy, whose surname this is.

clue.text: Cooked hash set all solid — must be long-standing

indicators.note: cooked suggests tampered with or rearranged, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A kitchen disaster: the hash has been left until it set hard, and has been sitting for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' rearranges the fifteen letters HASHSETALLSOLID.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something extremely old or established for a very long time.

clue.text: Undergarment conceals, to a certain extent, a boob

parts.note: half can mean partly, as in half-finished
a slip is a mistake, as is a boob

explanation.surface: A piece of underwear partly hides an embarrassing wardrobe malfunction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conceals' is a link here; 'boob' is a blunder, not anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-slip is a petticoat worn from the waist down, an item of underwear.

clue.text: One who get moving with King-Ace-King

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
taken as written
R again stands for rex, king

explanation.surface: A card player gets going with a hand of king, ace and king.
explanation.definitionFit: A racer is someone who moves fast, competing at speed.

clue.text: Came across a can containing nothing in the bottom

parts.note: to come across something is to find it

indicators.note: the can holds the next piece within it

parts.note: a tin is a can
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone discovered an empty can at the bottom of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' puts O inside TIN to give TION.
explanation.definitionFit: A foundation is the base or lowest part of a structure, hence its bottom.

clue.text: Framework of iron case rebuilt

indicators.note: the letters are put together again in a different order, as a structure rebuilt

explanation.surface: The structure of an iron casing has been reconstructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' rearranges IRONCASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is an outline of events or a plot, a framework for a story.

clue.text: Can hug getting out of bed

parts.note: a lock is a tight hold, as in a wrestler's hug
up means risen from bed

explanation.surface: A person can cuddle as they are getting up in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' is slang for prison, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A lock-up is a jail cell, and can is slang for a prison.

clue.text: Be upright with legs apart, or mess about with darts instead

indicators.note: to mess about with letters is to jumble them into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Advice to a pub darts player: plant your feet wide, or fool around with the darts instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess about' rearranges DARTSINSTEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand astride is to stand with one leg on each side, legs spread.

clue.text: Small rodent to stop and think about a hole

parts.note: to field is to stop the ball in cricket

indicators.note: the thinking word goes round the hole

parts.note: to muse is to think
O is shaped like a hole

explanation.surface: An instruction to pause and consider a hole in the ground, as a small animal might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stop' is the cricket sense: a fielder stops the ball. 'about' signals the hole going inside the thinking word.
explanation.definitionFit: A field mouse is a small wild mouse, a type of little rodent.

clue.text: Pop concert: one was played by Leslie Caron

parts.note: a gig is a pop concert
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pop concert where one star was the French actress Leslie Caron.
explanation.walkthrough: Leslie Caron took the title role in the 1958 film musical.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of the musical film was portrayed by actress Leslie Caron.

clue.text: Fellow sailor says Blair wants his tea stirred round

indicators.note: the letters are stirred like a cup of tea into a new order

parts.note: Tony Blair was PM, prime minister

explanation.surface: A sailor reports that Tony Blair likes his tea stirred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'says' and 'wants' are link words; 'stirred round' shuffles all three pieces as one pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipmate is a sailor serving on the same vessel, a fellow seaman.

clue.text: Talk affectedly at me first about the fruit mixture

indicators.note: the word me is placed before the word at

parts.note: to mince is to speak with affected daintiness

explanation.surface: Someone complains about prissy talk before they discuss a fruit mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts ME ahead of AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Mincemeat is a mixture of dried fruit, suet and spices used in mince pies.

clue.text: Angry about gear found in water

indicators.note: the angry word goes round the gear word

parts.note: irate means angry
rig is equipment or gear

explanation.surface: Someone is cross about kit discovered in water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water' is a verb here, not the liquid; 'about' signals the angry word wrapping the gear.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrigate is to water land by supplying channels of water.

clue.text: Governor puts messy oil rag in front of church

indicators.note: the jumbled letters come before the church piece
a messy arrangement of the letters gives a new order

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a dirty oily rag outside the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messy' rearranges OILRAG to OLIGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An oligarch is one of a small group who rule, a governor in that sense.

clue.text: Negative put next to green light in cubbyhole

parts.note: no is a negative
OK is approval, like giving the green light

explanation.surface: A refusal is placed beside a go-ahead signal in a little alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a small recess or corner, like a cubbyhole.

clue.text: Molested us in a bunk

indicators.note: the second piece sits inside the first

parts.note: abed means in bed, in a bunk

explanation.surface: A grim report of people interfered with while lying in a bunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bunk' stands for being in bed; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To be abused is to be maltreated or molested.

clue.text: A simple herb I fancy to be perennial

indicators.note: fancy suggests elaborate or reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener muses that a plain herb might keep coming back each year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges ASIMPLEHERBI.
explanation.definitionFit: Perennial means lasting forever, which is to say everlasting and never dying.

clue.text: Fruit tree for community leader

definitions.meaning: a small tree with dark berries
a senior figure with authority in a community

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the berry-bearing tree and a senior respected figure in a group.

clue.text: Composer to ask about Rattle's introduction

indicators.note: the asking word goes round the other letter

parts.note: to beg is to ask

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A composer is invited to discuss how conductor Simon Rattle opened a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside BEG. Alban Berg was an Austrian composer; Simon Rattle is a conductor, a scene-setting misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School.

clue.text: It's plain: a road follower must turn round

indicators.note: the whole string of pieces is turned to face the other way

parts.note: a nut is a fan or follower

explanation.surface: A simple statement that someone following a road has to turn back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must turn round' reverses ARDNUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is a vast treeless Arctic plain.

clue.text: Paid attention and fibbed about a machine gun

indicators.note: the fibbing word goes round the weapon

parts.note: lied means told fibs
the Sten was a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: Someone noticed a person lying about a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sten was a cheap British submachine gun of the Second World War; 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To have listened is to have heard carefully, giving attention.

clue.text: Net kept in loch for accessibility

indicators.note: the net word is held inside the loch

parts.note: Loch Ness is the famous Scottish lake
to net money is to earn it

explanation.surface: A fishing net held in a Scottish lake for easy reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Net' is a verb, to gain money, not a fishing net; 'kept in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearness is closeness, being easy to reach, hence accessibility.

clue.text: Senility makes chief magistrate display thanks

indicators.note: the magistrate shows the thanks word within his own letters

parts.note: the Doge was the chief magistrate of Venice
ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: An aged Venetian ruler shows gratitude in his old age.
explanation.walkthrough: Venice was ruled by a Doge; 'display' signals the ruler showing the thanks within him.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotage is the weakness of mind that comes with old age.
